lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Your window is on the right of a bottle. Where is the bright side, and what single shadow shape would you draw on the table?

FEEDBACK
The bright side faces the right-hand window, and the cast shadow is one shape stretching to the left. Draw that shape’s edges first. A shadow has a direction because the light has a direction. If you move the bottle, look again before you keep the old shadow.

WATCH FOR
Shadows should be scribbled all around the object, because shade is a mood rather than a shape caused by a light source.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

WORKED MODEL
Noah’s lamp is on the left, so one shadow shape stretches to the right of the mug. The left side of the mug is the bright side. On the table he sees a long bounded shape, not a fog, and he draws its outline before any dark filling. He describes his own lamp. He does not borrow a story about a gallery artwork.

TRY FIRST
Your window is on the right of a bottle. Where is the bright side, and what single shadow shape would you draw on the table?

FEEDBACK
The bright side faces the right-hand window, and the cast shadow is one shape stretching to the left. Draw that shape’s edges first. A shadow has a direction because the light has a direction. If you move the bottle, look again before you keep the old shadow.
teach_steps.explain:

The cast shadow is one shape on the table, with edges you can draw, and it falls on the opposite side from the light. WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.
